name: Norepinephrine
high_alert_note: Named as a vasopressor in the FDA infusion pump page's examples of high-risk infusions; the local high-alert list governs.
summary: Vasopressor used to raise blood pressure in adults with severe, acute hypotension. Nursing focus: infusion-site and tissue protection, avoiding abrupt interruption, and rhythm and pressure monitoring.
evidence_type_note: The evidence here is a regulator product label (prescribing information written for prescribers and pharmacists). It is not a bedside nursing practice guideline: the nursing actions are inferences from label warnings, marked partial, and the unit's protocol governs practice.
jurisdiction_note: US FDA label only. EMA, MHRA and SFDA labels were not read; indications, warnings and presentations differ by country and by manufacturer.

sources.use: regulator label sections (boxed warning, indications, warnings, adverse reactions) read in full text
FDA infusion pump page (high-risk infusion examples)

items.text: The label describes norepinephrine as a catecholamine indicated to raise blood pressure in adults with severe, acute hypotension.
The label advises infusing into a large vein, because extravasation can cause local tissue necrosis through vasoconstriction.
Check the infusion site and surrounding tissue for signs of extravasation or ischaemia, and report them at once.
Do not stop or interrupt the infusion without an instruction from the prescriber or protocol.
Frequency of blood pressure, heart rate and rhythm checks follows the unit's vasoactive infusion protocol.
Tissue ischaemia: avoid extravasation into the tissues because local necrosis can follow; management of an extravasation, including any infiltration treatment, is a prescriber or protocol decision.
Sudden cessation of the infusion may cause marked hypotension (label warning).
Cardiac arrhythmias and allergic reactions are listed among the label's warnings and precautions.
The label lists tissue ischaemia, hypotension after abrupt discontinuation and cardiac arrhythmias as the serious adverse reactions described in its warnings.
Escalate promptly for suspected extravasation, new arrhythmia, falling blood pressure or an interrupted infusion.
Record the infusion site checks, haemodynamic readings, pump checks and escalation per unit standard.
Use a structured handover (SBAR) when escalating.
Institution-specific preparation: follow your pharmacy's preparation standard and the product labelling. This library gives no preparation or concentration instructions.
Institution-specific dosing: follow the prescriber's order and your institution's approved protocol. This library gives no dosing instructions.

monitoring.text: Inspect the infusion site and surrounding skin for blanching, coolness or swelling.
Monitor blood pressure, heart rate and rhythm at the unit's frequency.
Keep the infusion running; do not interrupt it without an instruction.
Report suspected extravasation, arrhythmia or falling pressure immediately.
Record site checks, pump checks and responses.
